[XLA:CPU] Preserve safe custom fusion buffer reuse

Deny inferred buffer reuse for custom fusions unless their runtime
supports it. Preserve YNNPACK's existing HLO sharing rules and share
CpuAliasInfo between compilation and AOT loading.

Cover aliased oneDNN inputs through copy insertion and execution, plus
YNNPACK reuse. Keep the regression enabled on AArch64.

Signed-off-by: Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>

head_commit.message:
PR #52604: [XLA:GPU] Refresh the B300 target spec from a live B300

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52604

#ai-generated

Fixes #52602

### Status quo
`b300.txtpb` (from #34116, source device not stated) has 158 SMs, a 1.965 GHz clock, 297021865984 B of memory, 7.936 TB/s and a 135528448 B L2. A live B300 SXM6 AC reports 148, 2.032 GHz, 287416123392 B, 7.672 TB/s and 132644864 B. The spec also has no `name`, so `SpecMatchesLiveDevice` skips on B300, and it lacks the fields that the refreshed b200/gb300 specs carry.

### Why
Deviceless/AOT compiles for `GpuModel.B300` should see the same device as an on-device compile. With the current spec, for example, a bf16 elementwise kernel gets 128-bit vectors deviceless and 256-bit on device (65536 vs 32768 blocks for 2^26 elements).

### Design
- Regenerated from the `gpu_target_config.pbtxt` that `--xla_dump_to` writes on a B300 (jaxlib 0.12.1.dev20261108).
- Dropped the per-host fields `numa_node`, `pci_bus_id`, `kernel_mode_driver_version` and the top-level `runtime_version`. Of the checked-in specs, only vr_nvl72.txtpb has them.
- Kept `driver_version: "13.0.0"`, as in gb200/gb300/h100_sxm. `SupportsMovedChildCommands` reads it, so leaving it unset would turn moved child commands off for deviceless compiles.
- Kept `device_description_str: "NVIDIA B300"`, since `gpu_topology.cc` maps "NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC" to it.
- `name` is the live `NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC`.
- Version fields follow b200.txtpb: runtime/toolkit 13.2.0, cuDNN 9.23.0, CUB 3.1.2. The live machine had pip CUDA 13.5 and cuDNN 9.28.1, which describe the test environment rather than the device.
- Data only, no code change. #52432 adds memory bus width to other specs and does not touch this file; whichever lands second can add it here.

### Tests
- A deviceless JAX compile against the new spec gives the same `loop_add_fusion` launch (32768 x 128) as the live B300 does; the old spec gives 65536 x 128.
- The spec parses: deviceless compiles with it succeed.
- If the current values describe another B300 SKU, this should become a separate spec rather than a replacement (question in #52602).
- Not run: `CudnnDevicePropsTest.SpecMatchesLiveDevice` on B300 (needs a `--config=cuda` build). Only one B300 SKU (SXM6 AC) was available, so other B300 SKUs may report different values.

It also lacks the fields the other refreshed Blackwell specs carry. display_title: [XLA:GPU] Rename general, debugging, and Triton autotuner flags.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Rename general, debugging, and Triton autotuner flags.

Several autotuner flags carry legacy `gpu` or `gemm` prefixes even though they
apply to config assignment across backends or specifically target Triton
configs. Rename them to clearer, accurately scoped names:

- `--xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_backends` → `--xla_config_assigner_backends`
- `--xla_gpu_autotune_gemm_rtol` → `--xla_autotune_rtol`
- `--xla_gpu_dump_autotuned_instructions` →
  `--xla_dump_isolated_hlos_pre_and_post_config_assignment`
- `--xla_gpu_dump_autotune_logs_to` → `--xla_dump_autotune_logs_to`
- `--xla_gpu_override_gemm_autotuner` → `--xla_gpu_override_triton_config`
- `--xla_gpu_gemm_autotuner_override_file` →
  `--xla_gpu_override_triton_configs_file`

Add the new fields to `DebugOptions`, remove and reserve the old proto fields in
`xla.proto`, and keep the deprecated CLI flags as aliases that populate the new
proto fields for backward compatibility.

display_title: PR #52201: [XLA:GPU][Triton] Fix collective while-loop command buffer tests on ROCm

head_commit.message:
PR #52201: [XLA:GPU][Triton] Fix collective while-loop command buffer tests on ROCm

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52201

📝 Summary of Changes
On ROCm, where HIP graphs have no conditional nodes: CommandBufferConversionPass drops the WHILE command and captures the loop body into a command buffer nested inside the WhileThunk. The 20-collective while-loop tests for all-gather, all-reduce and all-to-all additionally asserted that the kWhile thunk itself is captured, which only holds on CUDA, so those two expectations are now guarded by Capability().IsCuda().

`CountThunksInDump` only tracked command buffer membership for top-level thunks, so thunks inside a nested kCommandBuffer were counted as being outside one. Track the indentation of the innermost enclosing kCommandBuffer instead.

🎯 Justification
On ROCm, the `Twenty*InWhileLoopWithCudaGraphs` multi-gpu single host triton collective op tests (`all_gather_e2e_test`, `all_reduce_e2e_test`, `all_to_all_e2e_test`) fail because HIP graphs have no conditional nodes.
These tests must therefore be adapted so that they pass on both Cuda and ROCm.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

display_title: [ROCm] [CUDA] Keep recorded collectives out of output allocations under VA remapping

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Gate collectives out of output allocations behind a flag

- Add xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs (default
  false). CreateMustNotLiveOut installs the predicate only when it is set.
- Do not match host send/recv: they lower to host send/recv thunks, which
  are never recorded.
- gpu_compiler_test checks maybe_live_out of the all-reduce's allocation
  instead of comparing temp allocation sizes.

display_title: PR #52104: [ROCm] [CUDA] Keep recorded collectives out of output allocations under VA remapping

head_commit.message:
PR #52104: [ROCm] [CUDA] Keep recorded collectives out of output allocations under VA remapping Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52104 Shared GPU code (CUDA and ROCm). This is mainly beneficial to ROCm, where re-recording a collective on every execution is costly. from CUDA side change is not regressive but not greatly beneficial either (Tested on B300). from ROCm side I'm trying find ways to reduce the recapture whenever possible this is one of the PR for that. ## 📝 Summary of Changes New flag `--xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` (default false). With it, `COLLECTIVES` in command buffers and `SKIP_TEMP` / `SKIP_PROFILED`, values that a collective which may be recorded defines or reads stay out of output allocations (`BufferAssigner::Options::must_not_live_out`). Host send/recv are not matched. GPU buffer assigner options are now built in `CreateBufferAssignerOptions`. ## 🎯 Justification ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Collective recorded in a command buffer
COLLECTIVES + SKIP_TEMP / SKIP_PROFILED + flag"] --> B{"Where is its operand / result?"} B -- "Before: output allocation (buffer reuse)" --> C["New address every execution"] --> D["Collective re-recorded
on every initialization"] B -- "After: temp allocation" --> E["Stable address"] --> F["Collective skipped
at initialization"] classDef bad fill:#fde2e2,stroke:#c0392b,color:#1a1a1a classDef good fill:#e2f5e6,stroke:#27ae60,color:#1a1a1a class D bad class F good ``` Trade-off: values that shared an output allocation now need temp space. Buffer assignment runs before the command buffer conversion pass, so the predicate also covers collectives that end up outside a command buffer (for example below `xla_gpu_graph_min_graph_size`). Off by default; `ALWAYS_UPDATE` (default) is unchanged. ## 🚀 Kind of Contribution ⚡️ Performance Improvement ## 🧪 Unit Tests - `gpu_memory_space_assignment_test`: 7 new tests (when the predicate is installed, including flag off; result and async collective-group placement, with a flag-off control; collectives filter; which instructions and positions match; host send/recv not matched; live-out result). - `gpu_compiler_test`: `CollectiveCommandBuffersKeepCollectivesOutOfOutputs` (`maybe_live_out` of the all-reduce's allocation under `ALWAYS_UPDATE`, and under `SKIP_TEMP` with the flag off and on). ## 🧪 Execution Tests `collective_ops_command_buffer_test` on MI355X: `SKIP_TEMP` and `SKIP_PROFILED` with the flag on give the same results as `ALWAYS_UPDATE`. The two `RaggedAllToAll` peer-access cases fail in every mode on this ROCm build (`InitializeCrossDeviceBarrier is not implemented`), independent of this change. B300 was tested on the previous revision, where the predicate was on whenever these modes were set. CreateMustNotLiveOut installs the predicate only when it is set. - Do not match host send/recv: they lower to host send/recv thunks, which are never recorded. - gpu_compiler_test checks maybe_live_out of the all-reduce's allocation instead of comparing temp allocation sizes. Merging this change closes #52104 COPYBARA_INTEGRATE_REVIEW=https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52104 from ROCm:fix/collectives-out-of-output-allocations-upstream 841452b0ed4617e51d1dfd0f561cd31fbecb0165 PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020866368

display_title: PR #52604: [XLA:GPU] Refresh the B300 target spec from a live B300

head_commit.message:
PR #52604: [XLA:GPU] Refresh the B300 target spec from a live B300

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52604

#ai-generated

Fixes #52602

### Status quo
`b300.txtpb` (from #34116, source device not stated) has 158 SMs, a 1.965 GHz clock, 297021865984 B of memory, 7.936 TB/s and a 135528448 B L2. A live B300 SXM6 AC reports 148, 2.032 GHz, 287416123392 B, 7.672 TB/s and 132644864 B. The spec also has no `name`, so `SpecMatchesLiveDevice` skips on B300, and it lacks the fields that the refreshed b200/gb300 specs carry.

### Why
Deviceless/AOT compiles for `GpuModel.B300` should see the same device as an on-device compile. With the current spec, for example, a bf16 elementwise kernel gets 128-bit vectors deviceless and 256-bit on device (65536 vs 32768 blocks for 2^26 elements).

### Design
- Regenerated from the `gpu_target_config.pbtxt` that `--xla_dump_to` writes on a B300 (jaxlib 0.12.1.dev20261108).
- Dropped the per-host fields `numa_node`, `pci_bus_id`, `kernel_mode_driver_version` and the top-level `runtime_version`. Of the checked-in specs, only vr_nvl72.txtpb has them.
- Kept `driver_version: "13.0.0"`, as in gb200/gb300/h100_sxm. `SupportsMovedChildCommands` reads it, so leaving it unset would turn moved child commands off for deviceless compiles.
- Kept `device_description_str: "NVIDIA B300"`, since `gpu_topology.cc` maps "NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC" to it.
- `name` is the live `NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC`.
- Version fields follow b200.txtpb: runtime/toolkit 13.2.0, cuDNN 9.23.0, CUB 3.1.2. The live machine had pip CUDA 13.5 and cuDNN 9.28.1, which describe the test environment rather than the device.
- Data only, no code change. #52432 adds memory bus width to other specs and does not touch this file; whichever lands second can add it here.

### Tests
- A deviceless JAX compile against the new spec gives the same `loop_add_fusion` launch (32768 x 128) as the live B300 does; the old spec gives 65536 x 128.
- The spec parses: deviceless compiles with it succeed.
- If the current values describe another B300 SKU, this should become a separate spec rather than a replacement (question in #52602).

head_commit.message:
PR #51750: Fix a use-after-free race in AcquireClique

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51750

📝 Summary of Changes

In AcquireClique, the rendezvous callback looks up a cached clique under state.mu, where it returns a raw LockableGpuClique* and called Acquire() after releasing the mutex. the only thing keeping the clique alive is its entry in state.cliques. Then a concurrent run on the same clique key could take state.mu, decide the clique's parent isn't a superset of its split_from, take safety_lock, erase the entry and destroy the clique. The first run would then call Acquire() on freed memory, a use-after-free.

🎯 Justification

A potential use-after-free crash

head_commit.message:
PR #52604: [XLA:GPU] Refresh the B300 target spec from a live B300

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52604

#ai-generated

Fixes #52602

### Status quo
`b300.txtpb` (from #34116, source device not stated) has 158 SMs, a 1.965 GHz clock, 297021865984 B of memory, 7.936 TB/s and a 135528448 B L2. A live B300 SXM6 AC reports 148, 2.032 GHz, 287416123392 B, 7.672 TB/s and 132644864 B. The spec also has no `name`, so `SpecMatchesLiveDevice` skips on B300, and it lacks the fields that the refreshed b200/gb300 specs carry.

### Why
Deviceless/AOT compiles for `GpuModel.B300` should see the same device as an on-device compile. With the current spec, for example, a bf16 elementwise kernel gets 128-bit vectors deviceless and 256-bit on device (65536 vs 32768 blocks for 2^26 elements).

### Design
- Regenerated from the `gpu_target_config.pbtxt` that `--xla_dump_to` writes on a B300 (jaxlib 0.12.1.dev20261108).
- Dropped the per-host fields `numa_node`, `pci_bus_id`, `kernel_mode_driver_version` and the top-level `runtime_version`. Of the checked-in specs, only vr_nvl72.txtpb has them.
- Kept `driver_version: "13.0.0"`, as in gb200/gb300/h100_sxm. `SupportsMovedChildCommands` reads it, so leaving it unset would turn moved child commands off for deviceless compiles.
- Kept `device_description_str: "NVIDIA B300"`, since `gpu_topology.cc` maps "NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC" to it.
- `name` is the live `NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC`.
- Version fields follow b200.txtpb: runtime/toolkit 13.2.0, cuDNN 9.23.0, CUB 3.1.2. The live machine had pip CUDA 13.5 and cuDNN 9.28.1, which describe the test environment rather than the device.
- Data only, no code change. #52432 adds memory bus width to other specs and does not touch this file; whichever lands second can add it here.

### Tests
- A deviceless JAX compile against the new spec gives the same `loop_add_fusion` launch (32768 x 128) as the live B300 does; the old spec gives 65536 x 128.
- The spec parses: deviceless compiles with it succeed.
- If the current values describe another B300 SKU, this should become a separate spec rather than a replacement (question in #52602).
- Not run: `CudnnDevicePropsTest.SpecMatchesLiveDevice` on B300 (needs a `--config=cuda` build). Only one B300 SKU (SXM6 AC) was available, so other B300 SKUs may report different values.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Rename general, debugging, and Triton autotuner flags.

Several autotuner flags carry legacy `gpu` or `gemm` prefixes even though they
apply to config assignment across backends or specifically target Triton
configs. Rename them to clearer, accurately scoped names:

- `--xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_backends` → `--xla_config_assigner_backends`
- `--xla_gpu_autotune_gemm_rtol` → `--xla_autotune_rtol`
- `--xla_gpu_dump_autotuned_instructions` →
  `--xla_dump_isolated_hlos_pre_and_post_config_assignment`
- `--xla_gpu_dump_autotune_logs_to` → `--xla_dump_autotune_logs_to`
- `--xla_gpu_override_gemm_autotuner` → `--xla_gpu_override_triton_config`
- `--xla_gpu_gemm_autotuner_override_file` →
  `--xla_gpu_override_triton_configs_file`

Add the new fields to `DebugOptions`, remove and reserve the old proto fields in
`xla.proto`, and keep the deprecated CLI flags as aliases that populate the new
proto fields for backward compatibility.

display_title: PR #52201: [XLA:GPU][Triton] Fix collective while-loop command buffer tests on ROCm

head_commit.message:
PR #52201: [XLA:GPU][Triton] Fix collective while-loop command buffer tests on ROCm

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52201

📝 Summary of Changes
On ROCm, where HIP graphs have no conditional nodes: CommandBufferConversionPass drops the WHILE command and captures the loop body into a command buffer nested inside the WhileThunk. The 20-collective while-loop tests for all-gather, all-reduce and all-to-all additionally asserted that the kWhile thunk itself is captured, which only holds on CUDA, so those two expectations are now guarded by Capability().IsCuda().

`CountThunksInDump` only tracked command buffer membership for top-level thunks, so thunks inside a nested kCommandBuffer were counted as being outside one. Track the indentation of the innermost enclosing kCommandBuffer instead.

🎯 Justification
On ROCm, the `Twenty*InWhileLoopWithCudaGraphs` multi-gpu single host triton collective op tests (`all_gather_e2e_test`, `all_reduce_e2e_test`, `all_to_all_e2e_test`) fail because HIP graphs have no conditional nodes.
These tests must therefore be adapted so that they pass on both Cuda and ROCm.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support CTA cluster synchronization in bitonic sort

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support CTA cluster synchronization in bitonic sort

Previously, the MLIR bitonic sort emitter only fused compare-and-swap steps
within one CTA's shared-memory tile (`tile_size`), requiring a separate global
kernel launch per step once `xor_mask >= tile_size`.

On Hopper+ GPUs (`sm_90+`), extend tiled bitonic sort across 2-CTA clusters
using distributed shared memory (DSMEM) and cluster barriers, doubling the
in-kernel sort span and cutting global round-trips:
- Propagate optional `se::ClusterDim` through `LaunchDimensions` and custom
  kernel specs to set driver cluster dims and `"nvvm.cluster_dim"` on kernels.
- Add `gpu::BarrierScope` (default `Workgroup`) to `xla_gpu.sync_threads`,
  forward it to `gpu.barrier` in `LowerTensors`, and lower cluster barriers to
  aligned `nvvm.cluster.arrive` and `nvvm.cluster.wait` in `LowerToLLVMGPU`.
- Support `"xla_gpu.dsmem"` on shared-memory accesses in `LowerTensors` by
  mapping the base pointer to the peer CTA's shared memory via `nvvm.mapa`.
- Emit 2-CTA clustered bitonic sort kernels when stages exceed `tile_size`,
  unclustered blocks exceed SM count, and cluster padding is at most 12.5%
  (capping at 2 CTAs avoids GPC fragmentation and register pressure). Cross-CTA
  steps use `gpu.cluster_block_id x` and DSMEM; full tiles keep the unrolled
  fast path while bounds-checked and post-cluster `kIntraTileSort` merges stay
  rolled.

head_commit.message:
PR #52104: [ROCm] [CUDA] Keep recorded collectives out of output allocations under VA remapping Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52104 Shared GPU code (CUDA and ROCm). This is mainly beneficial to ROCm, where re-recording a collective on every execution is costly. from CUDA side change is not regressive but not greatly beneficial either (Tested on B300). from ROCm side I'm trying find ways to reduce the recapture whenever possible this is one of the PR for that. ## 📝 Summary of Changes New flag `--xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` (default false). With it, `COLLECTIVES` in command buffers and `SKIP_TEMP` / `SKIP_PROFILED`, values that a collective which may be recorded defines or reads stay out of output allocations (`BufferAssigner::Options::must_not_live_out`). display_title: PR #51750: Fix a use-after-free race in AcquireClique

head_commit.message:
PR #51750: Fix a use-after-free race in AcquireClique

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51750

📝 Summary of Changes

In AcquireClique, the rendezvous callback looks up a cached clique under state.mu, where it returns a raw LockableGpuClique* and called Acquire() after releasing the mutex. the only thing keeping the clique alive is its entry in state.cliques. Then a concurrent run on the same clique key could take state.mu, decide the clique's parent isn't a superset of its split_from, take safety_lock, erase the entry and destroy the clique. The first run would then call Acquire() on freed memory, a use-after-free.

🎯 Justification

A potential use-after-free crash

🚀 Kind of Contribution

Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix

display_title: PR #52443: [XLA:GPU] Add support probe and dense fallback for cuDNN ragged-dot fusion

head_commit.message:
PR #52443: [XLA:GPU] Add support probe and dense fallback for cuDNN ragged-dot fusion

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52443

📝 Summary of Changes

Make the cuDNN ragged-dot fusion fall back to the regular dense expansion when
cuDNN cannot build a plan for a given ragged dot. The fusion stays behind
`xla_gpu_experimental_use_ragged_dot_fusion`, whose default is unchanged.

- `RaggedDotRewriter` takes an optional `is_supported_by_cudnn_fusion` callback.
  A ragged dot that passes the existing static gates (cuDNN version, Ampere+,
  binary libraries enabled, unbatched 2D lhs / 2D-3D rhs / 1D group sizes,
  F16/BF16 types, single ragged dim) is only left for the fusion rewriter if
  the callback also returns true; otherwise it is expanded to dense dot as before.
  The decision has to be made here because `RaggedDotRewriter` runs before layout
  assignment, while `RaggedDotFusionRewriter` runs post-layout, where a dense
  expansion would produce layout-less ops.
- New `IsRaggedDotSupportedByCuDnn` (`ragged_dot_cudnn_support.{h,cc}`, CUDA-only):
  builds a scratch module with the ragged dot, runs `RaggedDotFusionRewriter`,
  and asks cuDNN about the resulting fusion via `ResolveCudnnSupport` +
  `GetAvailablePlanCount(...) > 0`, for both JIT and deviceless compilation
  (honoring `xla_gpu_cudnn_deviceless_compilation_mode`). Only a positive answer
  counts as supported; no plans and errors all fall back to dense, with the
  reason logged at `VLOG(3)`.
- Plumbing: virtual `GpuCompiler::IsRaggedDotSupportedByCuDnn` (default
  `Decision::Forbid`, overridden in `NVPTXCompiler`). `RunOptimizationPasses` now
  receives the `StreamExecutor*` and derives `is_deviceless` from it.

🎯 Justification

With `xla_gpu_experimental_use_ragged_dot_fusion` enabled, a ragged dot that
passes the static gates but that cuDNN has no engine for (e.g. mixed
token/weight dtypes) fails compilation hard in the cuDNN fusion compiler. With
this change such a ragged dot compiles via the dense path instead, so the flag
can be turned on safely later.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A.

🧪 Unit Tests:

- `RaggedDotRewriterTest.CudnnSupportCallbackDecidesFusionOrExpansion`: with the
  fusion enabled, a callback returning true leaves the ragged dot in place; a
  callback returning false expands it to dense.
- `RaggedDotRewriterTest.ExpandsWhenBinaryLibrariesDisabled`.
- `ragged_dot_cudnn_support_test`: supported and unsupported ragged dots.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use named barrier 1 for single-block phase transitions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use named barrier 1 for single-block phase transitions.

This prevents `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` errors when generalizing MultiStageFusion to column reduction and transpose that emit block barriers themselves.

In `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion`, consecutive single-block phases synchronize via `bar.sync 0` across all `max_threads` of block 0, while partial-CTA sub-kernels (`sub_threads < max_threads`) rewrite intra-phase barriers to `barrier.sync 0, sub_threads` on the same hardware barrier 0. When a partial-CTA reduction or transpose runs as a single-block phase followed by another single-block phase, threads with `tid >= sub_threads` skip the sub-kernel and reach the trailing `bar.sync 0`, arming barrier 0 with thread count `max_threads` while active threads arrive at barrier 0 with thread count `sub_threads`, raising `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020202243

name: CI
display_title: Retry buffer assignment with direct operand reuse only

head_commit.message:
Retry buffer assignment with direct operand reuse only

The heap simulator lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand that it only reads through other positions (e.g. a `bitcast` or a `get-tuple-element`). This lowers the peak memory, but the reused buffer has to stay at the same offset for longer, which makes it harder to pack. For some modules the fragmentation therefore grows by more than the peak memory shrinks.

So this change makes the fallback in `BufferAssigner` try all its strategies a second time without this kind of reuse (`HeapSimulator::Options::may_reuse_operand_buffers_through_other_positions`) if none of them fits the memory limit. As before, each color keeps the assignment with the lowest memory usage. This way a module that is close to its memory limit does not need more memory than it would without the reuse through other positions.

Nothing changes for modules where one of the existing strategies fits. For the others, the fallback now runs twice as many heap simulations.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020813629

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate dimensions and overflow in `xla::ifrt::Shape::NumElements`

`xla::ifrt::Shape::num_elements()` multiplied dimension sizes without checking for negative dimensions or `int64_t` overflow, allowing shapes constructed outside `Shape::FromProto` to wrap `int64_t` modulo 2^64 or return negative or canceled-sign element counts.

Add `Shape::NumElements()` returning `absl::StatusOr<int64_t>` when any dimension is negative or the element count overflows `int64_t` (reused by `Shape::FromProto` and `ifrt_proxy`'s `ArrayMemRegion::FromZerothElementPointer`), and update `Shape::num_elements()` to `CHECK_OK` on `NumElements()` while keeping `Shape(absl::Span<const int64_t>)` zero-overhead at construction time.

Existing `Shape` tests only checked overflow in `Shape::FromProto` and small non-negative dimensions in `Shape::num_elements()`.

display_title: [IFRT] Add absl_nonnull to RCReference aliases and API pointer arguments

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Add absl_nonnull to RCReference aliases and API pointer arguments

IFRT reference-counted handle aliases (`ArrayRef`, `BundleRef`, `ValueRef`, and `DeviceListRef`) and core IFRT API pointer arguments (such as `Device*` and `LoadOptions` in `Client`, `Client*` in deserialization helpers and `IfrtIrProgramCompiler`, and `SerDes` in `RegisterSerDes`) are required by contract to be non-null, yet lacked compile-time nullability annotations.

Mark `RCReferenceWrapper` with `ABSL_NULLABILITY_COMPATIBLE` (with matching nullability-annotated RTTI overloads in `rtti.h`), add `absl_nonnull` to `ArrayRef`, `BundleRef`, `ValueRef`, `DeviceListRef`, and non-null pointer arguments across IFRT interfaces, and mark `DeserializeExecutableOptions` in `Compiler::DeserializeLoadedExecutable` `absl_nullable`.
